summary: A real four-process Gloo reproduction confirms the base TP-first ordering fails on unseeded TP source rank 2. The candidate's CP-first ordering also fails, on unseeded CP source rank 1. The candidate mock passes because it supplies payload to non-sources without jointly modeling the source process and omits the failing rank combination.

tests.what_was_measured: Real four-process Gloo groups matching attn_tp_size=2 and attn_cp_size=2 reproduced len(None) on global rank 2, the source of TP group [2,3].
The candidate's mocked regression and adjacent scheduler tests pass (8 passed), but do not jointly model all ranks in a collective.
Real four-process Gloo groups show the candidate still raises len(None), now on global rank 1, the source of CP group [1,3].

gpu_execution.evidence: The assigned host has one AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 GPU, but the reviewed collective tests intentionally used CPU Gloo. The original topology requires at least four participating ranks and its reported full server command uses eight GPUs.

remaining_counterexamples: With attn_tp_size=2 and attn_cp_size=2, global rank 1 (attn_tp_rank=1, attn_cp_rank=0) is the source of CP group [1,3] but starts with data=None; candidate CP-first ordering calls broadcast_pyobj there and raises TypeError from len(None).
remaining_limitations: The original eight-GPU DeepSeek-V4 serving command was not run because only one gfx950 GPU was assigned and model weights were unavailable.
No NCCL, DSV4 semantic, full-model, or multi-node validation was possible; the deterministic four-process Gloo reproduction covers the Python object-broadcast contract and exact rank topology.
No native rebuild was needed because the candidate changes only Python and tests.
